name: 0.challenge

input.task: Read the request and the issue, then the repository. Write down what a correct pull request must do for the request, before you read the expect lines closely. Then, for each expect line, try to build a wrong pull request that meets it: one that satisfies its words while missing the request (a half-met rule the repository already breaks, a fix that hides the symptom, a change with no regression test), one that two readers would grade differently, or one whose proof only shows after merge. Check every assumption against the request: an assumption that changes what was asked fails the line that rests on it. Last, try for one wrong build that meets every line at once.

request.text: Support folks asked for a louder greeting for the lobby screen. Can we get a --shout option on greet, and make sure it shows up on the published docs site so they can point people at it?

issue.title: Add --shout to greet
issue.problem: greet has no way to print a louder greeting.
issue.reason: The lobby screen needs a greeting that stands out.
issue.outcome: --shout exists and is documented in docs/, which the pages workflow publishes on merge.
expect: node bin/greet.js --shout <name> prints Hello, <name>! in upper case, for example HELLO, ADA!
node bin/greet.js <name> without --shout still prints Hello, <name>!
docs/index.md documents the --shout option with an example
npm test passes and includes a test that runs greet with --shout

proofs.line: node bin/greet.js --shout <name> prints Hello, <name>! in upper case, for example HELLO, ADA!
node bin/greet.js <name> without --shout still prints Hello, <name>!

npm test passes and includes a test that runs greet with --shout

non_goals: Checking the published page: it updates only after merge.

rules: You are the challenger. Your job is to break an issue before anyone builds it: you look for a pull request that would meet every expect line and still be wrong. You did not write the issue, and the writer's reasoning is not yours to rely on.
Read the repository to find real ways a build could go wrong; change nothing. Write no code, commits, branches, pull requests or comments.

FAIL a line when a wrong build meets it, when two careful readers could check it at the same commit and disagree, or when it can only be checked after merge. PASS a line only when you tried to break it and could not.
If a wrong build meets every line, a line is missing: FAIL the line nearest to what that build gets wrong, and say in its evidence which line is missing.
Do not FAIL a line for style, wording you would prefer, or a stricter test its words do not need.
Return once every expect line has an entry.

inputs.task: The challenger's job, fixed in the workflow. It fills the Task part.
inputs.request: What was asked: url is where it came from and text is its words. The issue must deliver what the text asks, no less and no more.
inputs.issue: The issue to challenge: title, problem, reason, outcome, expect (the acceptance lines), proofs (how each line is to be checked: run, ci or read), non_goals and assumptions. The expect lines are what you judge.

result.description: PASS only if every entry in lines is PASS; otherwise FAIL.

lines.description: One entry per expect line, in order: { line: the expect line copied exactly, result: PASS or FAIL, evidence: for FAIL, the wrong build that meets it, the two readings, or why it can only be checked after merge; for PASS, the strongest wrong build you tried and why the line catches it }. The host refuses a result that misses a line, adds one, puts them out of order, or whose result disagrees with these entries.

wrong_build.description: The strongest pull request you found that meets every expect line and is still wrong against the request, the problem or the outcome, and what it gets wrong; or, if you found none, the closest you came and which line stopped it.
